newsitem.title: FINLAND: OUTOKUMPU SEES COPPER STOCKS RISING AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: OUTOKUMPU SEES COPPER STOCKS RISING AGAIN.

text.p: Finnish mining and metals group Outokumpu Oy said on Monday currently very low copper inventories were likely to rise again towards the end of 1996.

"Copper was the only Outokumpu-produced base that showed some growth in consumption from 1995, whereas the consumption of nickel and zinc declined," Outokumpu said in a statement with its January-August results.

"Copper inventories are at a very low level at the moment, but increasing supply toward year-end is predicted to result in growth in inventories. Nickel and zinc inventories are still higher than normal."

Describing a 304 million markka operating loss at its base metals division over the period as "weaker than expected", Outokumpu blamed low metal prices and 61 million markka in inventory losses, plus special charges in the second tertial.

It said cathode copper production at the Zaldivar mine in Chile, in which Outokumpu owns a 50 percent stake, had increased slower than scheduled and total 1996 output would reach 75,000 tonnes. It earlier saw this at 85,000 tonnes.

"The mine will reach its full capacity level of 125,000 tonnes per year in 1997," Outokumpu said, adding that while the mine showed an operating profit for the period it was loss-making at the net level.

Although copper prices fell sharply -- with copper on average down 19 percent and nickel down five percent year-on-year in January-August -- Outokumpu said treatment and refining charges had increased to some extent with rising copper and zinc mine production.

In stainless steel, where the average German transaction price fell 16 percent from the first to the second tertial, Outokumpu said "market conditions have remained unchanged except for a slight decline in prices".

Demand increased in late summer and prices "are expected to increase to some extent during the autumn, especially in Europe", Outokumpu said, adding inventories at both distributors and end-users are believed to be close to normal levels.
Copper products demand remained fairly good after a weak start to the year, Outokumpu said.

"The average prices of copper products ... were somewhat higher than the corresponding 1995 prices," it said. "The business area's net sales, however, failed to increase because of a marked decline in the price of copper metal."
